lines: A module is delivered more than once inside a single page:
tasks-main: 3,834 B beyond the first copy, @vueuse/components 3,091 B, @vueuse/shared 743 B.
All 3 pages load the same 2 files: 1,419,204 B raw, 358,547 B gzip, 99.5 % of the smallest page (tasks-talk, 1,426,161 B).
Inside: moment 292,987 B, @nextcloud/vue 259,906 B, @nextcloud/timezones 124,994 B, ical.js 74,964 B, @nextcloud/calendar-js 70,046 B.
moment, 292,987 B on the tasks-main page: carries its locale data; luxon and date-fns are a fraction of it.
core-js, 31,038 B on the tasks-main page: polyfills for browsers older than the build targets.
vite-plugin-node-polyfills, 29,400 B on the tasks-main page: Node APIs polyfilled into a browser bundle.
No package is imported as a whole: every package contributes only the modules that are used (70 packages, 541 modules).
On this measure the form of importing is exhausted. A root import whose barrel the bundler removes completely leaves no trace, so this is evidence, not proof.
No bundler chunk in js and css is left without something that loads it.
